relations.statement: s (n+1) = s n - d n + b n with d n <= s n
relations.hypotheses: hd: forall n, d n <= s n; hs: forall n, s (n+1) = s n - d n + b n

lemmas.statement: Under hd, hs and hb (d n < b n for all n), s 0 + n <= s n for all n; births b are an input, not derived.
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem supply_growth (s d b : ℕ → ℕ) (hd : ∀ n, d n ≤ s n) (hs : ∀ n, s (n + 1) = s n - d n + b n) (hb : ∀ n, d n < b n) : ∀ n, s 0 + n ≤ s n := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    have h1 := hs k
    have h2 := hd k
    have h3 := hb k
    omega

near_misses.claim: If only d n <= b n, then s 0 + n <= s n
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Constant supply with d n = b n gives s n = s 0, so growth by n fails for n > 0.

near_misses.claim: Strict births exceeding discharges gives growth without hypothesis d n <= s n
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Natural subtraction truncates at 0, so s n - d n is not s n minus d n when d n > s n; the accounting identity is not preserved.

open_obligations: Births b are a host input; Genesis does not derive them.
